title: Automated TLS Lifecycle for Global Retail Logistics
business: A global logistics provider managing thousands of microservices across distributed Kubernetes clusters.
problem: Manual certificate rotation leads to frequent service outages and security compliance failures when certificates expire unexpectedly.
solution: Implementing cert-manager to automate the issuance and renewal of TLS certificates via integration with HashiCorp Vault, ensuring that every workload receives a valid, short-lived certificate without manual intervention.
steps: Install cert-manager into the cluster using Helm to manage the lifecycle of Certificate resources.
Configure an Issuer or ClusterIssuer resource to define the connection parameters for the HashiCorp Vault PKI backend.
Define a Certificate resource for each microservice, specifying the common name, DNS names, and the reference to the Issuer.
Mount the resulting Kubernetes Secret containing the TLS key and certificate into the application Pods for secure communication.
outcome: The organization achieves continuous service availability and consistent security posture by eliminating human error in the certificate renewal process.
limitation: The standard Certificate resource stores private keys in Kubernetes Secrets, which are accessible to users with read access to the namespace; this can be checked by auditing RBAC permissions on Secret objects.

To replace HashiCorp Vault with a native Kubernetes certificate authority.
